entries.claim: cds CLI provides init, add <facet>, watch, compile, build, up; cds watch is a shortcut for 'cds serve all --with-mocks --in-memory?'; Java uses 'mvn cds:watch'

Production facets: cds add hana | xsuaa | mta | multitenancy | ias; regenerate XSUAA descriptor with 'cds compile --to xsuaa' after auth annotation changes; xs-security.json uses scopes and role-templates with $XSAPPNAME

Declarative authorization via @requires and @restrict [{grant,to,where}]; Fiori UI via @UI.LineItem/@UI.SelectionFields; field control via @mandatory/@readonly/@UI.Hidden; @title/@description map to @Common.Label/@Core.Description
Node.js handlers registered via this.before/this.on/this.after; req exposes event/target/query(CQN)/data/user/tenant; queries via cds.ql (SELECT/INSERT/UPSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)

CAP Java handlers are @Component classes implementing EventHandler with @ServiceName, using @Before/@On/@After; context.proceed() is valid only in @On handlers; queries via CQN builders and PersistenceService
UI5 Tooling is distributed as @ui5/cli providing the 'ui5' command (init, serve, build); the project is described by ui5.yaml (specVersion, metadata, type, framework)
manifest.json is the application descriptor with three namespaces: sap.app, sap.ui, sap.ui5; sap.ui5 declares dependencies, models, rootView, and routing (routes/targets)
SAPUI5 uses MVC with XML views (mvc:View referencing controllerName) and controllers extending sap.ui.core.mvc.Controller; models include JSONModel, OData V2/V4 ODataModel, and ResourceModel for i18n

SAP Fiori tools is an extension pack (SAPSE.sap-ux-fiori-tools-extension-pack) for VS Code and SAP Business Application Studio to build Fiori elements apps; includes Application Generator, Application Modeler (Page Map), Guided Development, and annotation tooling

Apps are generated via @sap/generator-fiori (Yeoman, supports headless config); the fiori CLI from @sap/ux-ui5-tooling provides fiori run / fiori add / fiori deploy; mock preview uses the sap-fe-mockserver middleware via ui5-mock.yaml

The ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) is the core of ABAP Cloud for clean-core apps; a RAP business object = CDS data model + behavior definition/implementation + service definition + service binding (typically OData V4); managed vs unmanaged implementation types

RAP behavior building blocks are determinations, validations, and actions, implemented in a behavior pool via ABAP EML (READ/MODIFY ENTITIES) with failed/reported structures; developed in ABAP Development Tools (ADT) for Eclipse
Clean core / ABAP Cloud requires consuming only Released APIs (API State visible in ADT), no modifications, custom code in the customer namespace, and the ABAP for Cloud Development language scope

Modern ABAP CDS uses DEFINE VIEW ENTITY (replacing legacy DEFINE VIEW ... WITH); associations declared with 'association [card] to Target as _Alias on ...' and consumed via path expressions and $projection
Row-level authorization is declared in DCL access controls (define role ... grant select on <View> where ... = aspect pfcg_auth(...)); the view opts in with @AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK
CDS views are tested with the CDS test double framework (cl_cds_test_environment) which replaces underlying tables with test data for deterministic ABAP Unit tests
